svg.text: Arbiter service lifecycle — what bedrock-d actually does to the boxes
the arbiter "services" = bedrock-rqlited-arbiter + bedrock-weed-filer, the .254 VIP, the mgmt-master role — all riding the one `cluster` DRBD mount
verdict LOSE, and the device is frozen → nothing can be stopped cleanly

g.text: 1 · drbdsetup secondary --force=yes (~0 s)
EIO the held writes, force role → Secondary. DEMOTE FIRST — the one op that must be fast.
2 · SIGKILL the holders (by service name)
bedrock-rqlited-arbiter + bedrock-weed-filer.
dirty pages DROPPED by the kernel on death → minority STILL never writes.
3 · umount -l (lazy)
detach the mount without touching the frozen FS → open count drops to 0.
NEVER: systemctl stop · umount · resume-io
all three block forever on a frozen FS, and resume-io would let the
minority write — re-opening the exact bug the freeze prevents.
4 · reconnect as Secondary → resync from winner
after-sb-0pri discard-zero-changes → UpToDate. Done.

svg.text: verdict WIN (or it already held the role and never lost it)

g.text: 1 · drbdadm primary cluster
already-UpToDate, peer Outdated → instant; no resync needed to serve.
2 · mount /var/lib/bedrock/cluster
the rqlite data dir + filer state ride this one DRBD volume.
3 · bring up the .254 cluster VIP (/32)
advertised via the path-vector route layer; clients follow it.
4 · start bedrock-rqlited-arbiter + bedrock-weed-filer
on the data that was already replicated to this node.
5 · assume the mgmt-master role
serves the control plane; CA, dashboards, sagas follow the mount.
often: nothing moved at all
if the old master was the winner (e.g. it lost only a Secondary),
it just exit-4-resumes and keeps every service. No transfer.
